name: Kuwait
summary: Muslim estates follow Sharia fixed shares under the Personal Status Law of 1984. Non-Muslim communities may use their own law, but what applies to a non-Muslim foreigner was not confirmed. Kuwaiti law reportedly does not recognise trusts, and private foundations are not available.
reserved_share: Muslims: Sharia fixed shares under the Personal Status Law (Law 51 of 1984), which covers inheritance; the share rules and the one-third bequest limit were not retrieved.
foreign_law_note: Non-Muslims may ask family courts to apply their community's own customary or religious law (reported); the rule for foreign non-Muslims was not found. Non-GCC heirs who inherit Kuwaiti real estate must sell within a year unless permitted (reported).
trust_note: Kuwait Times reports that Kuwaiti law does not recognise trusts and recognises only sole ownership; a directory page says the opposite, so this is low-confidence. Charitable foundations are regulated by a June 2025 regulation (at least 10 Kuwaiti founders, KD 10,000 deposit) and are not private family foundations. Waqf exists.
open_questions: Law 51/1984 article on non-Muslims (art. 334 was suggested) not retrieved.
Conflicting sources on whether trusts are recognised; confirm with Kuwaiti counsel.
Kuwait's Civil Code conflict rule for foreigners' succession not found.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.
